summary: Rebecca Redwood French is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Washington and Yale University. Her career includes posts at the University of Colorado Boulder (attested 1996–2003) and the University at Buffalo (attested 2014).
Rebecca Sundén works in the fields of Indology and Tibetology. She studied at the University of Hamburg, where she is attested as a Wissenschaftliche Projektmitarbeiterin in 2026.

Reginald A. Ray is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. Educated under teachers including Mircea Eliade and Chögyam Trungpa, he taught at the University of Colorado Boulder (attested 2001–2002) and Naropa University (attested 2001–2006).
Reginald Edward Enthoven (1869–1952) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his education at Wellington College (~1883–1887) and New College (1887).

Reginald Heber (1783–1826) was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at Brasenose College and the University of Oxford (~1800–1823), later serving as a Fellow at All Souls College, Oxford, in 1805.

Reginald Stephen Copleston (1845–1925) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar educated at Exeter College and Merton College. He served as a Fellow at St John's College, Oxford (1870–1875) and President of the Royal Asiatic Society of Sri Lanka (~1876–1902).
Rei Yoshimura (b. 1929) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He was educated at Waseda University, where he also served as a professor (attested 1996).
Reiho Masunaga (1902–1981) worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied under Kaiten Nukariya and served as a teacher at Komazawa University (attested 1956).

Reiko Ohnuma is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at UC Berkeley and the University of Michigan under Luis Oscar Gómez and Padmanabh S. Jaini. She held positions at UT Austin, the University of Alabama, and Dartmouth College.

Reimon Yuki (1902–1992) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Daijō Tokiwa. He held posts at the Academy of Oriental Culture, the Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia, Kyoto Women's University, and Ryukoku University.

Reiner Wiehl (1929–2010) was a philosopher who studied at the University of Nancy and Goethe University Frankfurt. He served as Professor of Philosophy at the University of Hamburg (1969–1977) and Heidelberg University (appointed 1977).

Reinhold F. G. Müller (1882–1966) worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Berlin, Innsbruck, and Greifswald, later serving as an assistant at the University of Greifswald (~1909–1911) and PD in medicine at the University of Leipzig (1942).
Reinhold Grünendahl is an Indologist. He held positions at the Free University of Berlin (attested 1983–1984) and the Göttingen State and University Library (attested 2008).

Reinhold Klotz (1807–1870) was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Leipzig, where he subsequently served as an assistant professor (1832) and extraordinary professor (1849–1870).

Reinhold Niebuhr (1892–1971) was a religious studies and philosophy scholar. He studied at Elmhurst University, Eden Theological Seminary, and Yale Divinity School, later serving on the faculty at Union Theological Seminary from ~1928 to 1960.

Reinhold Rost (1822–1896) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. Educated at Jena under Johann Gildemeister and Johann Gustav Stickel, he served at St Augustine's College, Canterbury, King's College London, the Royal Asiatic Society, and as Librarian of the India Office.

Reinhold Trautmann (1883–1951) was a linguist who earned his Ph.D. at Königsberg under Adalbert Bezzenberger. He held professorships at the German University in Prague, Königsberg, Leipzig, and Jena, and headed an institute at the GDR Academy of Sciences.

Reinhold von Stackelberg (1860–1907) was a linguist and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. He studied at Tartu, Leipzig, and Strasbourg, later serving as Privatdozent at Leipzig (1891–1892) and Professor of Persian at the Lazarev Institute (1894).
Reirin Yamada (1889–1979) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He was educated at Komazawa University and later served as president of Komazawa Junior College.
Remeen Firoz is an Indology scholar who studied as a PhD student at the Australian National University under the doctoral supervision of Assa Doron (attested 2026).
